questions.stem: What must be confirmed at the Stop Before You Block step of a peripheral nerve block?
When describing an ultrasound-guided nerve block, what two things must you state about the probe?
When describing a nerve block, what should you state about the needle?
questions.answer: Needle length, insertion site, in-plane or out-of-plane and direction

questions.stem: In a peripheral nerve block, after negative aspiration for blood, what initial volume is injected?
In a peripheral nerve block, what aliquot size is used when continuing the injection slowly?
If the needle needs repositioning during a peripheral nerve block, what should you do?
questions.answer: Reposition the needle and inject further volume with the same checks

questions.stem: After a peripheral nerve block, which dressing is suggested once the needle is removed?
In the general peripheral nerve block technique, what is Step 3?
In the general peripheral nerve block technique, Step 4 is to ____ the transducer position or needle insertion point.
In the general peripheral nerve block technique, how many methods identify the correct needle position at Step 5?
In the general peripheral nerve block technique, what should aspiration at Step 6 show?
In the general peripheral nerve block technique, what should Step 7 injection not produce?
Which ultrasound probe frequency suits a nerve block target less than 2cm deep, such as wrist or ankle?
Which ultrasound frequency suits a nerve block target 2-4cm deep, such as interscalene or femoral?
Which ultrasound frequency suits a nerve block target 4-10cm deep, such as popliteal or infraclavicular?
Which ultrasound frequency suits a nerve block target more than 10cm deep, such as coeliac ganglion block?
Superficial, high frequency (5-13 MHz) probes that suit most nerve blocks are ____ probes.
Which probe type, used for ankle and elbow blocks, has a small footprint and narrower field?
Which probe shape is low frequency and deep with a wide field, used for sciatic block?
Why does an echogenic needle appear brighter on ultrasound?
questions.answer: Its etched, cross-hatched shaft scatters more of the beam back to the probe

questions.stem: A nerve can be imaged in a short-axis view or a ____ view.
On ultrasound, nerves look round, oval or triangular, and are hyperechoic or ____.
How do you confirm on ultrasound that a structure is the nerve you think it is?
questions.answer: Slide the probe along it, cephalad-caudad

questions.stem: In a pre-block ultrasound scan, what should the planned needle path avoid?
How does a needle's brightness on ultrasound change as it runs closer to parallel with the probe face?
What should stay in view at all times while advancing a needle for a nerve block?
In a peripheral nerve block, what volume of dextrose or LA is injected to locate the needle tip?
How should a needle be advanced when crossing fascia during a nerve block?
questions.answer: Slowly, then wait for a pop or give

questions.stem: In ultrasound-guided nerve blocks, what is hydrodissection?
options: Aspirating fluid to confirm needle position
Injecting a test dose to exclude intravascular needle
Injecting contrast to show the block spread
Injecting fluid on purpose to separate tissue planes

questions.stem: When injecting local anaesthetic around a nerve, which two things should be avoided?
In the local anaesthetic injection step of a nerve block, what volume is injected after aspirating?
When injecting around a nerve, aim for ____ spread, also called doughnut or halo.
Which technique keeps the needle still for large-volume plexus and major nerve blocks?
In continuous nerve blocks, why are catheters hard to see on ultrasound?
For a continuous block, how far past the tip must you go before needle, nerve and catheter never share a plane?
What is the best check of catheter tip position in a continuous nerve block?
When testing a nerve block catheter, what volume is injected through it?
If no distinct pops are felt during needle advance for a nerve block, what should you do?
questions.answer: Withdraw, recheck landmarks, change angle or entry point

questions.stem: In a peripheral nerve block, what does bone contact during needle advance suggest?
options: The probe frequency is too low

questions.stem: In a peripheral nerve block, if blood returns on aspiration, how long should you press on the site after removing the needle?
During a nerve block, what should you do if there is resistance to injection?
Signs of local anaesthetic toxicity include circumoral ____, tinnitus, dizziness and seizure.
If a nerve block gives no pain relief after 30 minutes, what should be done next?
questions.answer: Give a further 20 ml of low-concentration LA, or consider other analgesia
